_hinweis: Gebaut von werkzeuge/eden_rise/sturm_eden_rise.py - dort aendern. Regeln: kern/sturm.py.

anker.text: Double the mooring lines and watch the anchor chain all night.

strom.text: Switch off everything that can wait and keep the batteries alive.

kombuese.text: Lash down everything that can fly and keep something hot going.

beiboot.text: Haul the tender up and lash it down on the swim platform.

notloesung.text: Check the makeshift power line rigged yesterday before the rain gets into it.

bitte.chiara: Put me on the anchor watch, First Officer. My father taught me to hear a chain slipping before you can feel it, and I haven't forgotten.
bitte.rosi: I'm taking the power, Officer, don't even think about giving it to someone else. And yesterday's patch - somebody who didn't build it should look at it, because I'll only see what I meant to do.
bitte.lea: I could do the tender in my sleep, honestly, I've lashed it down a hundred times. But could I take the anchor? Just once I'd like to do the thing that actually matters.
bitte.lola: Boss, if the galley's not locked down, there'll be knives flying around down there. Put me where the pots are - I'm useless with ropes, I swear.
bitte.maxwell: Mr. Maximum will carry the tender up the stairs if he has to, brother. Lines, chains, anything heavy - just point, and he lifts it.

chiara.anker: The anchor. Thank you. I'll sit on that chain all night if I have to.
chiara.strom: The power? I - fine. Rosi will have to tell me which switches not to touch.
chiara.kombuese: The galley. Alright, I can lash down a galley, I've done it in worse weather than this.
chiara.beiboot: The tender, then. I'll check Lea's knots twice and hope that's enough.
chiara.notloesung: Yesterday's repair? I can watch it, First Officer, but I wouldn't know a bad joint if it bit me.

rosi.strom: Good. Nobody touches my batteries tonight, not even Megan.
rosi.notloesung: My own patch? Fine. But I'll be checking my own work, Officer, and that's never as good as it sounds.
rosi.anker: The anchor. Me. Out in the rain. You do know I'm an electrician, right?
rosi.kombuese: The galley? You want me in the galley. Lola, I'm sorry in advance.
rosi.beiboot: The tender. Okay. I'll do my best, and my best with boats is not great.

lea.anker: The anchor? Really? Okay. Okay, I won't let it go, I promise.
lea.beiboot: The tender. Easy. I'll have it up and lashed before the first drop of rain.
lea.kombuese: Galley, got it. I'll help Lola - or I'll just do what she does, only faster.
lea.strom: Power? Um. I suppose I'll write down everything Rosi says.
lea.notloesung: The repair? I can watch it, but if it sparks I'm not sure what I'd actually do.

lola.kombuese: My galley! Yes, Boss. Nothing's flying anywhere tonight, I'll glue the pans to the wall if I have to.
lola.anker: The anchor? Oh. Right. Is that the - yeah. Yep. I'll figure it out, mate.
lola.strom: Power, me? Boss, I make toast. I don't make electricity.
lola.beiboot: The tender, okay, so that's the little boat. I know that much. Cool. Cool.
lola.notloesung: The repair thing? I'm going to be honest, Boss, I don't know which end is the dangerous one.

maxwell.beiboot: The tender! Mr. Maximum accepts. He will carry it, he will tie it, and if it panics he will sing to it.
maxwell.anker: The anchor watch. Mr. Maximum against the chain, man against metal. The chain will lose, brother.
maxwell.kombuese: The galley. Mr. Maximum respects the galley. He will hold the fridge shut with one hand.
maxwell.strom: Power? Brother, Mr. Maximum trusts muscles, not cables. But fine. He will guard the switches.
maxwell.notloesung: The repair. Mr. Maximum will stare at it very hard until it behaves.

ruhe.chiara: I'm resting? Tonight? Fine. But if you need me, you knock, First Officer. You don't wait.
ruhe.rosi: You're sending me to bed in a storm. Officer, you're either very clever or very stupid.
ruhe.lea: Oh. Rest. Okay. Maybe - yeah, maybe that's not a bad idea, actually.
ruhe.lola: Sleep? In this? I'll be up anyway, Boss, so at least I'll make tea for whoever's still alive at five.
ruhe.maxwell: Mr. Maximum, on the bench? He will do push-ups in his cabin in protest. Quietly.

auftakt: Forty knots by midnight, the forecast says. I'd like to see how your crew handles that, Duc. I'll stay out of the way, and I will take notes.
There's a storm coming in tonight, and I'm not leaving before it does. So show me your crew, Duc. Who goes where?
Gusts to forty knots after midnight. On paper this is a good crew. I want to see what it looks like at three in the morning.
auftrag: Five jobs, and six people if you count yourself. Put everyone where you want them, Duc, and someone gets to sleep.
plan_stark: That's a plan, Duc. Everyone where they know what they're doing. Let's see if it survives the night.
plan_gemischt: Some of that makes sense. Some of it I'd have done differently. We'll find out which part is which.
plan_schwach: Interesting choices, First Officer. I'll write them down exactly as you made them.
selbst: You're taking a post yourself. Then you can't run anywhere else tonight - you know that, I hope.
frei: You're keeping yourself free. Fine. One of you can run tonight, so make sure you run the right way.
los: Alright. Everyone knows their job. Go.
nacht: Here it comes. Nobody does anything heroic unless they have to.
ok: Good. That's what I wanted to see.
They didn't even look round for you. That's a crew.
knapp: It held, Duc. Not pretty, but it held.
weg: That's going to cost someone money.
And that, First Officer, is what happens when nobody is where they should be.
sprint: You ran the right way. Good.
Hm. You picked your moment, Duc.
ende_gut: Dawn, everyone still aboard, nothing on the rocks. I came to see a crew, Duc, and I saw one.
ende_mittel: You got through. Not cleanly, but you got through. That's exactly how it goes in my notes.
ende_schlecht: Look at this deck, First Officer. Then look at your crew. I've seen what I needed to see.

lea_anker: Lea's got the anchor? Good on her.
She'd better not fall asleep on it.
She won't. Mr. Maximum has seen her eyes. Like a hawk. A small, wet hawk.
lea_nicht: She wanted the anchor, you know. She asked for it.
She'll survive. It's a storm, not a birthday.
Still. Somebody should tell her why.
ruhe: Somebody gets to sleep through this? Lucky.
Bet they don't sleep a wink.
Mr. Maximum sleeps through anything. Earthquakes. Weddings.
standard: Forty knots. In this bay. Wonderful.
The batteries will hold if nobody does anything stupid.
So something stupid, then, just to be sure?

boee: Everybody grab something! Mr. Maximum has the cushions!
My herbs! Somebody save the basil!
rufe: I've got candles! Do candles count?
Mr. Maximum can see in the dark! He cannot. He is lying.

boee.text: The first gust lays the yacht over. Rain comes in sideways, and everything on deck that isn't tied down starts to move.
boee.ok: For a minute everyone is pulling, catching, tying. Then the deck is clear, and you're all soaked and grinning.

kombuese.text: A crash from below. The galley lurches, and the pot rack swings loose.
kombuese.ok: Down in the galley, nothing moves that shouldn't.
kombuese.knapp: It's a mess down there, but nothing is broken.
kombuese.weg: Plates, jars and half the coffee end up on the floor. Breakfast will be cold.
kombuese.duc_ok: You catch the pot rack before it comes down and lash it with a tea towel and a belt.
kombuese.duc_knapp: You wedge yourself against the fridge and hold on. Something breaks, but not much.
kombuese.sprint: You take the stairs three at a time and throw your weight against the swinging rack.

beiboot.text: A wave lifts the swim platform. The tender jerks against its straps.
beiboot.ok: The tender sits tight on the platform, strapped down twice.
beiboot.knapp: The tender bangs against the stern twice, then it's caught.
beiboot.weg: A strap snaps. The tender slams into the stern before anyone catches it, and the hull takes a dent.
beiboot.duc_ok: You get a second strap across the tender and haul it tight with your foot against the hull.
beiboot.duc_knapp: You throw a line over the tender and hold it until the wave passes. It scrapes, but it stays.
beiboot.sprint: You slide down the wet stairs to the platform and grab the loose strap with both hands.

strom.text: The lights flicker, then go out. Only the red emergency strip is left.
strom.ok: One by one the essentials come back: fridge, pumps, anchor light.
strom.knapp: The batteries hold, just, but everything except the anchor light stays dark.
strom.weg: The batteries run down to nothing. The rest of the night is cold, dark and loud.
strom.duc_ok: You shed every load you can find by torchlight, and the batteries settle.
strom.duc_knapp: You switch off what you can find in the dark. The batteries sink, then hold.
strom.sprint: You feel your way down to the power room by the red strip and start pulling breakers.

notloesung.text: Water runs down the cable from yesterday's repair. Something hisses in the dark.
notloesung.ok: The wet joint is found in time, cut off and taped dry.
notloesung.knapp: It sparks once, then holds under three layers of tape.
notloesung.weg: The fix shorts out with a bang and a smell of burnt plastic. The cable and the breaker are gone.
notloesung.duc_ok: You find the wet joint by its smell before it shorts, cut the power to it and tape it dry. It holds.
notloesung.duc_knapp: You get there as it sparks and kill the breaker. Dark, but nothing burns.
notloesung.sprint: You run for the hissing cable and yank the breaker before it can catch.

anker.text: The chain groans. The rocks of the bay are closer than they were an hour ago.
anker.ok: The chain holds. The yacht swings back into the wind and lies easier.
anker.knapp: The anchor drags a few metres, bites again and holds.
anker.weg: The anchor drags. By the time the engine pulls her clear, the keel has scraped rock.
anker.duc_ok: You let out more chain at exactly the right moment, and the anchor bites.
anker.duc_knapp: You start the engine and ease her forward until the chain stops groaning.
anker.sprint: You run forward along the rail, rain in your face, to the groaning chain.

ok.chiara.anker: The chain's holding! I've let out ten more metres, she's lying easier now!
ok.maxwell.anker: Chain is holding, brother! Mr. Maximum has it, and it has learned respect!
ok.rosi.strom: Everything we don't need is off. Fridge, pumps and the anchor light - that's all we feed tonight. We'll make it to morning.
ok.lea.beiboot: Got it! Second strap's on, it's not going anywhere!
ok.maxwell.beiboot: Mr. Maximum has hugged the tender. The tender has stopped moving.
ok.lola.kombuese: All good down here! Everything's lashed and the kettle's on - nobody panic, there'll be tea!

knapp.chiara.beiboot: It's holding, just about! I need another pair of hands on this strap!
knapp.chiara.kombuese: Most of it's still in the cupboards. Most.
knapp.rosi.notloesung: It's sparking at the joint - hold on - there. Taped. It won't win a prize, but it's holding.
knapp.lea.anker: It's dragging a bit - no, no, it's caught again! I think it's caught! I'm not letting go!
knapp.lea.kombuese: The pot rack came down, but I caught the big one! Mostly with my shin.
knapp.maxwell.kombuese: Mr. Maximum is holding the fridge shut. He cannot let go. Please send snacks.

panik.chiara: I can't see what's wrong, First Officer! I need someone who knows this!
panik.rosi: This isn't my thing, Officer! It's slipping, I can't hold it!
panik.lea: Duc! Duc, I don't know what to do, it's - please!
panik.lola: Boss! Boss, I can't - I don't know what I'm doing!
panik.maxwell: Brother! Mr. Maximum is strong, but he is not smart enough for this one!

hilfe.chiara: Thank God. Show me, and I'll do the rest.
hilfe.rosi: Officer! Finally. Hold this, and don't let go.
hilfe.lea: You came. Okay. Okay, I've got this end.
hilfe.lola: Boss! Oh, thank God. Tell me what to grab.
hilfe.maxwell: Number One! Together, then. On three!

gut: Did we - did we actually do that?
Mr. Maximum never doubted it. Mr. Maximum doubted it a little.
Not bad, everyone. Really not bad.
mittel: We're still floating. That's the good news.
And the bad news is the list on Megan's clipboard.
I need a coffee the size of my head.
schlecht: Don't look at the bill, Officer. Just don't.
I keep hearing that chain. Every time I close my eyes.

morgen.chiara: I didn't sleep. Of course I didn't. But I'm fresh, so give me the worst job of the morning.
morgen.rosi: I slept two hours and fixed three things in my head. Coffee first, then I'll fix them for real.
morgen.lea: I actually slept! I feel terrible about it. Here - I made everyone toast.
morgen.lola: Tea for the survivors! And bacon. Don't ask where I found bacon.
morgen.maxwell: Mr. Maximum is rested and ashamed. As penance, he has made breakfast for everyone.

kombuese.text: Cold breakfast, broken jars: crew morale −1

beiboot.text: Dent in the tender's hull: €60 repair

strom.text: A cold, dark night: crew morale −1

notloesung.text: Burnt cable and breaker: €80 for parts

anker.text: Keel scraped on rock: €120 for the diver
